subject: Clarify: default retention for requests / generated outputs & deletion options
messages:
From: Lucy Bright <lucy@brightbank.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Quick question on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Ben / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our security team have one last set of clarifying questions about your default data retention model before we move forward:

1) When a hosted API request is made, what exactly is stored by default? Are prompts (the input) treated the same as generated outputs?
2) What is the default retention window for request/response artifacts in the hosted product (not Dedicated/Private)?
3) For EU-based tenants, are the stored artifacts kept in-region, and if so how long before deletion propagates across backups/replicas?
4) Is there an API or console flow our team can call to request deletion of specific sessions/requests?

We need language we can include in a procurement appendix and a short checklist for security review. If you have a one-pager or a quick matrix it would be super helpful.

Thanks,
Lucy
Security Architect, BrightBank

BrightBank (procurement@brightbank.com)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Lucy Bright <lucy@brightbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on what Redwood keeps by default (requests vs outputs)

Lucy — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front, then details and next steps below.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Hosted (Redwood API): by default we retain request metadata + request text (prompts) and generated outputs for 30 days.
- Generated outputs are classified as "derived content" but are retained for the same window by default on hosted; streaming fragments are ephemeral during the session and are not persisted once the session closes.
- EU tenants on hosted use regionally-resident storage for retained artifacts; deletion requests propagate to active storage within 48 hours and to backups/replicas within up to 30 days.
- Customers can request per-request opt-out at call-time (opt_out_persistence=true), or submit deletion requests via the Console or API (Delete-Request endpoint). Private/Dedicated customers can opt for zero-retention configurations.

Detailed notes
1) What we store by default
- Request metadata: timestamps, route, model version, token counts (used for billing/diagnostics) — retained 30 days.
- Request text (prompts): stored as part of the request artifact — retained 30 days by default.
- Generated outputs (full responses): retained 30 days on Hosted. Treated as generated artifacts, separate from aggregated telemetry (see below).
- Telemetry/metrics: aggregated traces and anonymized token-level stats are retained longer for quality and SLO monitoring (default 13 months, aggregated, no raw text).

2) Residency and deletion propagation (EU specifics)
- For customers electing EU residency, all default-retained artifacts are stored in EU regions only.
- Soft delete/propagation: once we action a deletion, objects in primary stores are removed within 48 hours. Backups/replication layers are on a rolling schedule and full propagation to all backup media can take up to 30 days. We provide a deletion certificate once completed.

3) Deletion controls available to customers
- Per-request opt-out parameter: include opt_out_persistence=true in the request header to avoid storing request/response artifacts for that call. (Note: metrics/billing counters still record counts.)
- Console data deletion: select sessions/objects and request removal — admin flow with audit trail.
- Delete-Request API: programmatic endpoint to remove specified request IDs or session IDs. Deletions produce an audit ticket id.
- Private & Dedicated: options to configure zero or shorter retention (customer-managed policies).

4) What customers should expect for procurement language
- We can provide the following appendix text (editable):
  • Redwood will retain request and generated output artifacts in hosted products for a default period of 30 days.
  • Customers may opt out of retention per-request or require zero-retention via dedicated/private deployments.
  • EU-resident data are stored in-region; deletion requests remove artifacts from primary storage within 48 hours and from backups within up to 30 days.

Attachments: I've attached a short cheatsheet and the Delete-Request API spec. I'm happy to transform that into a short appendix paragraph for your procurement team.

- Karhtik: can you prep a 10-minute walk-through of the Console delete flow for Lucy?

Lucy — adding a couple of procurement/legal clarifications that often come up:

- Billing records & invoices: we retain minimal billing line items for 24 months for accounting/audit (these do not contain full request/response text).
- Regulatory hold: if BrightBank requests a preservation order for an investigation, there is a documented legal hold process — preservation pauses deletion until a release request is received. We surface legal hold impacts in the Console.
- Deletion certificates: security teams often request a signed deletion certificate for compliance; we provide a machine-signed certificate when the delete propagation completes (primary + backup window).

I'll add an editable appendix paragraph and a short checklist for your security reviewer and push to the HubSpot deal and shared Drive link Ben referenced.

Marissa Cole
